# Timer display

> Overview type `timer` (since 1.0). Entity: required, a `timer` entity. Card type `custom:houseview-timer-overview-card` (widget type `timer_overview`), screensaver `type: timer`.

A black full-screen countdown for a Home Assistant `timer.*` entity: a ring of 60 orange tick marks around a rounded
square, the time left in large white figures and, beneath it, the length of the timer in small orange capitals
(`15 MIN`).

Unlike the weather overview it is an **event** overview: it appears over the dashboard **by itself** while the timer is
running, and goes away by itself when the timer finishes or is cancelled. A tap on it only closes it (the dashboard
underneath is untouched, nothing is pressed, and the timer keeps running); it stays closed until the timer has stopped
and been started again. It also works as a page card or a standalone card
(`custom:houseview-timer-overview-card`; a tap on the card opens the timer's more-info dialog).

You do not have to configure it: every `timer` widget on a carousel shows it automatically (the `timer_display` card
option, on by default). Write an explicit entry to choose a timer that has no widget, or to switch one timer off:

```yaml
type: custom:houseview-card
cards:
  - type: custom:houseview-clock-card
  - type: custom:houseview-timer-card
    entity: timer.kitchen_timer
screensaver:
  type: timer
  entity: timer.kitchen_timer
```

It is an automatic display: it is not offered in the editor's screensaver list. (A `screensaver` entry of type `timer` written in
YAML still works and can share the list with idle overviews, for example a weather scene that starts after 2 minutes.) If another screensaver is on screen when the timer starts, the timer display replaces it.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| entity | entity | required | A `timer.*` entity |
| name | text | none | Used for the screen reader label only (the display has no title) |

The framework keys apply (`enabled`, `preview`, `start_in_edit_mode`) with one difference: **`idle_timeout` is accepted
but ignored**, because an event overview is never started by idle time and takes no part in the round robin.
`preview: true` shows it at once whatever the timer does, for choosing the look in the editor. It does not appear while
the camera grid or the timer alarm is showing, or in edit mode (unless `start_in_edit_mode`). Starting a timer from a
HouseView widget brings it up (a pending service call does not hold it back).

## What is shown

| Timer state | Time | Caption | Ticks | Over the dashboard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | counts down to `finishes_at` | `15 MIN` | lit in proportion to the time left | comes up, until it ends |
| `paused` | `remaining` | `PAUSED · 15 MIN` | as when it was paused | stays up |
| `idle` | the duration (card only) | `READY` (card) | all dim | goes away |
| unavailable | "Timer unavailable" (card only) | | all dim | goes away |

* An `active` timer whose `finishes_at` is already in the past (stale data after a sleep, a late `idle`) counts as over:
  the display does not come up for it.
* **Time**: `m:ss`, `h:mm:ss` from one hour up, never negative, in tabular figures so the digits do not jitter. It is
  recomputed once a second from the clock.
* **Caption**: the timer's `duration`: `15 MIN`, `45 SEC`, `1 MIN 30 SEC`, `1 H 30 MIN`, `1 H`.
* **Ticks**: `ceil(60 * time left / duration)` ticks are lit, counted clockwise from the top centre, so the used-up
  (dim) ticks are the last ones: time is consumed counter-clockwise from the top. A timer extended beyond its duration
  keeps a full ring. Without a `duration` attribute the ring uses the longest length the entity's data proves.

## Cost

Painted with CSS only (a black box, 60 small rounded bars and two lines of text): no images, gradients, filters or
animation, so it makes no difference between `performance` modes and has no motion to reduce. The only JavaScript is
the once-a-second text and tick update on the shared ticker.
